prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and so showing how exporting, foreign investment and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: one part, B010, credited to Helpman and Melitz. What changed is the citation, which is narrower and now names exporting and foreign investment as well as reallocation. I considered a two-part configuration. Under the three-person cap, B010 uses two names, so a second part could add only one person. B003 and B019 would each need at least two more names to be coherent, which would mean dropping a name that B010 needs. I see no principled split, so I keep a single part. On merit, Melitz (2003) is a discovery with a distinct mechanism. Productivity differences across firms give a selection cutoff for exporting. Liberalisation then moves market share toward more productive firms, and aggregate productivity rises through reallocation, a channel that does not exist in representative-firm models. Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extends the same logic to the choice between exporting and foreign investment. These predictions are not implied by the 2008 new-trade-theory framework with symmetric firms. They concern exporter premia, entry and exit, and within-industry reallocation, and they have been tested on firm-level data for more than twenty years. I read the broad opening agreement on the pair only as evidence that attribution is stable across assessors, not as a measure of merit. The chair asked whether the qualitative result survives departures from Pareto. As I recall the literature, the existence of the selection cutoff, the exporter premium and the reallocation gain do not need Pareto draws. Pareto mainly gives closed-form aggregate welfare formulas, and I recall work showing the magnitude of the gains is sensitive to such assumptions. I have not verified this against sources. This is why I would word the citation around the mechanism and not around any welfare number.
statement.case_against: The reservations I take most seriously are as follows. First, credit: Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn contributed facts, parallel models or the firm-dynamics base, and a two-name award cannot honour them. This is a real cost. The citation wording and the scientific background should acknowledge them, and I would not widen the laureate set to cover them. Second, the quantitative size of the selection gains depends on distributional assumptions. Third, field balance after the 2008 trade prize, which I do not treat as decisive but which the Committee should weigh openly. Fourth, B010 is partly a theory-plus-evidence synthesis, so a critic could say its core is a tractable model that organised facts others documented. I disagree, because the model supplied the mechanism and the testable predictions. But that view is not unreasonable. Fifth, my own preference for the clean, identifiable discovery may undervalue B019's foundational mechanism or B003's broad empirical-methods influence. My field is matching and mechanism design, not trade, so I rely on my reading of the literature and have not independently verified the record.

responses.point: Boppart keeps B019 (Kiyotaki and Moore) as his preferred part because it is a single mechanism with two clear originators. He treats B010 as a serious alternative whose precursor credit is harder to settle.
responses.response: I agree that B019 has the cleaner two-author credit line, and the Committee should count that. We differ on the second criterion, how directly the mechanism has been confronted with data. For B010, selection and exporter premia were checked against firm-level data across many countries, and the qualitative predictions held. For B019, as you and several colleagues concede, the amplification channel is identified more indirectly, and 2022 is adjacent. On precursor credit, I think B010's problem is less severe than it looks. The selection-and-reallocation model is identifiably Melitz's and Helpman's, while the other contributions are parallel or motivating, which is a different thing from co-authorship of the same discovery. I keep B019 as an alternative and would not oppose it if the Committee judges the 2022 overlap to be small. I would not rank it above B010 on the present evidence.

responses.point: Strömberg moved to Kiyotaki and Moore alone, prefers B019 on the substance and durability of the idea, and says he is not fully settled on the order of B019 and B010.
responses.response: Dropping Gertler is the right call. The two-name boundary makes B019 much more defensible than your opening proposal. I agree the 2022 prize covered banks and runs, while Kiyotaki-Moore concerns collateral values and asset-price feedback. But the thematic adjacency remains a cost that a citation would have to address explicitly, and B010 does not carry it. Where I weigh evidence differently is that you value the mechanism's durability and I value how many independent tests it has survived. You say you are unsettled on the order, so I see our disagreement as narrow. If the Committee wants a macro-finance part, B019 with the two originators is the form I could support. I still put B010 first because its identification record is more direct.

responses.point: Hassler credits B003's Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes core as the cleanest credit structure on an empirical-methods entry. He asks whether B003 should be framed as a methods award or a substantive discovery, and he keeps it as his main alternative.
responses.response: That is the question that kept me from ranking B003 higher than an alternative, despite putting it first in my opening. The BLP contribution is a method with a real conceptual core: demand estimation with unobserved product characteristics, with endogenous prices handled by instruments and a tractable aggregation of random-coefficient demand. It is standard in antitrust, merger review and regulation. I would be comfortable calling that a discovery about how to measure market power and welfare. It is more tool than theory, and the Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin boundary is harder than B010's. I think a Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes trio would be defensible but would still be contested. Under the three-person cap it cannot be combined with B010, so it stays an alternative. I agree with you that the unified conceptual advance is what separates B010.

responses.point: Enflo narrowed B032 to Autor, Hanson and Dorn after discussion, and puts causal evidence on adjustment costs ahead of the trade model's attribution. She names B010 as her main alternative.
responses.response: Dropping Katz made the B032 attribution much more defensible, and I think the trade-shock work is the best identified and most attributable core of that literature. I still rank it below B010 for two reasons, which you flag yourself. The persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects and the shift-share identification behind them are still being re-examined, while B010's qualitative predictions have been repeatedly confirmed. B032 is also closer to a strong empirical programme on one episode than to a general mechanism. Your point that continued debate shows scrutiny and not fragility is fair, and I do not read the debate as a flaw. I would weigh it as maturity not yet fully settled. If the Committee wants a labour-economics part, your three-name set is the one I could accept. I keep B032 below my two alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee accepts a narrow citation that leaves out Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn and Redding, and whether acknowledging them in the scientific background is enough. I would exclude Redding because his main contribution is quantitative and spatial trade built on this framework, and no member has argued that he is co-core.

Whether the Committee sees B010 as a distinct advance from the 2008 prize. I think it is, because of the selection and reallocation channel and its testable predictions, but Boppart's concern is not fully answered.

How much the size of the gains from trade depends on distributional assumptions. I recall that the qualitative selection and reallocation result does not depend on Pareto draws, but I have not verified this.
Whether B003 or B019 should be preferred if the Committee puts more weight on a single clean credit line than on a larger body of confirming evidence, and if B019 is judged distinct from 2022.
My assessments rely on my own recollection of the literature and have not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. It shows no co-authorship or institutional tie to Helpman, Melitz, Kiyotaki, Moore, Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn or the other credited names on B010, B003 or B019. Disclosed for transparency only: I am an SSE affiliate alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and my research in matching, auctions and mechanism design is not the field of the preferred prize. Friberg's research in international trade is field-proximate to B010, and Strömberg's in corporate finance is field-proximate to B019. Neither is a credited candidate. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
